newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan paper says hostages health deteriorating.
newsitem.headline: Japan paper says hostages health deteriorating.

text.p: The health of hostages held at the Japanese ambassador"s residence in Lima has deteriorated, with growing cases of high blood pressure, asthma and depression, a Japanese newspaper reported on Monday.

The Asahi Shimbun, quoting members of a Peruvian Health Ministry and International Red Cross medical team carrying out daily checks on the 72 hostages, warned there was a growing risk of stomach ulcers among the captives as the siege entered its third month.

"We fear that if the incident drags on, inflammations and other diseases already present among the hostages will get worse and there may be a sudden outbreak of stomach ulcers or other stress-related conditions," the newspaper quoted a medical team member as saying.
Some hostages need treatment for more serious conditions such as cancer and diabetes, the paper reported.
The Asahi said around 20 hostages were suffering from high blood pressure, another 10 people had asthma and 18 of the 24 Japanese hostages had mild clinical depression.
The paper said test results on blood and urine samples taken 10 days ago also showed some hostages had developed abnormally high cholesterol levels.
About 15 members of the leftist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) took over the residence on December 17, initially holding hundreds of hostages.
Most of the hostages have been released but the rebels, who have demanded the release of imprisoned comrades, are still holding 72 key captives.
